channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: UN demands Israel immediately releases flotilla activists
item.description: The United Nations has called on Israel to immediately release two activists detained on a flotilla bound for Gaza. Israel has not commented on the UN's demand. The activists were detained on a ship attempting to reach Gaza.

item.title: World Cup Dynamic Ticket Pricing Drives Argentine Soccer Fans To Extremes
item.description: Argentina's soccer fans face high ticket prices at the World Cup due to dynamic pricing. The tournament has become the most expensive in history, prompting fans to seek extreme measures to obtain tickets. Many fans are struggling to afford tickets.

item.title: Trump threatens Iran with ‘higher level’ bombing if it doesn't reopen Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran has expressed interest in a "comprehensive agreement" with the US. The Strait of Hormuz has been virtually shut since February 28, blocking about 20% of world oil supplies. The strait has ‌been virtually shut since the conflict began on February 28 with air attacks on Iran ‌by ⁠the U. S.

item.title: Iran is now a superpower; ties with India are flourishing: Iran Foreign Ministry spokesperson
item.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Mr. Baqaei, stated that Iran's ties with India are flourishing. He also mentioned that Tehran is reviewing America's response to its peace proposal. The proposal aims to improve relations between Iran and the US.

item.title: CNN founder Ted Turner, a brash and outspoken television pioneer, has died at age 87
item.description: Ted Turner, the founder of CNN and a television pioneer, has died at the age of 87. He transformed an Atlanta TV station into a satellite-based "superstation" and founded the first 24-hour news network, CNN. Turner was known for his outspoken personality.

item.title: 3 strokes of caning for bullying: Singapore’s radical new rule for boys
item.description: Singapore has introduced a new rule imposing three strokes of caning for bullying. The rule specifically targets boys and aims to curb bullying behavior in schools. The punishment is part of a broader effort to maintain discipline and safety in Singapore's education system.

item.title: Iran war angle in White House dinner shooting? US probes motive behind Cole Tomas Allen’s attack
item.description: US authorities are investigating the motive behind Cole Tomas Allen's attack at a White House dinner, with some speculating about a possible Iran angle. Allen, a 29-year-old man, was shot by Secret Service agents after attempting to breach the event.

item.title: Ceasefire in a page: US, Iran shrink war to a memo
item.description: The US and Iran have agreed to a ceasefire, with the terms outlined in a single-page memo. The agreement marks a significant shift in the conflict, with both sides seeking to reduce tensions.

item.title: Four killed in post-election violence in India’s West Bengal
item.description: Four people were killed in post-election violence in India's West Bengal, where the ruling BJP won the state election for the first time. The unrest has gripped the key eastern state, with reports of clashes between supporters and opponents.

item.title: How I Got My Career in Foreign Policy: Liana Fix
item.description: Liana Fix, a foreign policy expert, has spoken about her career path in a recent interview. Fix, a Council on Foreign Relations fellow, has worked on various international projects and has written extensively on global issues.

item.title: Leo XIV Is the First Pope From the U.S. He’s Making That an Asset.
item.description: Pope Leo XIV, the first American pontiff, has used his papacy to challenge Washington, defying concerns about his election. A year into his role, Leo has shown a willingness to take a more assertive stance on global issues.

item.title: India's Paytm forecasts higher revenue growth in FY 2027
item.description: The company expects an increase in revenue, though specific targets have not been disclosed, indicating a positive outlook for the financial year. India's Paytm forecasts higher revenue growth in FY 2027.

item.title: Israeli strikes on Lebanon kill 4 despite ceasefire
item.description: Israeli strikes on Lebanon killed four people, occurring despite a ceasefire. The strikes have resulted in casualties, highlighting the ongoing tensions in the region. Israeli strikes on Lebanon kill 4 despite ceasefire.

item.title: Indonesia’s new(ish) aircraft carrier: defence boost or expensive gamble?
item.description: Indonesia is set to acquire its first aircraft carrier, the Giuseppe Garibaldi. The Indonesian Naval Chief stated it will be used for non-war military operations, aiming to boost maritime capabilities.

item.title: CNN Founder And TV News Trailblazer Ted Turner Dies At 87
item.description: Ted Turner, founder of CNN and a pioneer in 24-hour cable news, has died at 87. CNN launched in 1980 under his leadership, revolutionizing news consumption. CNN launched in 1980 as the first 24-hour cable news network.

item.title: Pioneering CNN founder Ted Turner dies at 87
item.description: Ted Turner, founder of CNN, died at 87. He launched CNN in 1980 as the first 24-hour news outlet, changing the landscape of news broadcasting. Ted Turner founded CNN as the first 24-hour news outlet in 1980.

item.title: Who is Zack Polanski, UK Greens leader and rising political star?
item.description: Zack Polanski, leader of the UK Greens, is gaining attention for his blend of environmental and socialist policies. He has drawn comparisons to Zohran Mamdani, a rising star in New York politics.

item.title: Former PAP MP Ong Ah Heng dies aged 84
item.description: Ong Ah Heng, a former PAP MP, has died at 84. He served three terms in Nee Soon Central SMC from 1997 to 2011. He was a three-term MP for Nee Soon Central SMC from 1997 to 2011.

item.title: Greetings from a sea village in Indonesia, where Indigenous fishing gets help from mangroves
item.description: The Indonesian village of Torosiaje is benefiting from mangroves to support Indigenous fishing. Colorful stilted houses in the village are perched over the Molucca Sea. As a water taxi rounded a corner at sunset, the village of Torosiaje came into view, with its colorful stilted houses perched over the Molucca Sea.

item.title: F1 and Sky agree five-year extensions to UK and Italy broadcast deals
item.description: F1 and Sky have agreed to five-year extensions for UK and Italy broadcast deals. The terms of the agreements have not been disclosed. F1 and Sky agree five-year extensions to UK and Italy broadcast deals.
